questions.prompt: What must a Go test file be named, and what is a test function's signature?

options.text: A file ending in `_test.go`, with `func TestXxx(t *testing.T)`
Any file, with `func test_xxx()`
A file named tests.go, with `@Test` annotations
spec.go, with `describe()` blocks

questions.explanation: Tests live in `_test.go` files as `func TestXxx(t *testing.T)` and run with `go test`.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `t.Error` and `t.Fatal`?

options.text: `Error` records a failure but continues; `Fatal` stops the current test
They are identical
`Fatal` continues; `Error` stops the test
`Error` is only for benchmarks

questions.explanation: `t.Error`/`Errorf` mark a failure and keep going; `t.Fatal`/`Fatalf` mark it and stop the current test immediately.

questions.prompt: A benchmark function is `func BenchmarkXxx(b *testing.B)` and loops `for i := 0; i < b.____; i++`.
questions.explanation: The framework adjusts `b.N` until timing is stable; you loop that many times, run with `go test -bench`.

options.text: With an `// Output:` comment it is run and its output is verified, and it appears in docs
It is ignored by the test runner
It only compiles but never runs
It replaces the need for TestXxx

questions.explanation: Example functions with an `// Output:` comment are compiled, executed, checked against the comment, and shown in the package documentation.

questions.prompt: Which are idiomatic Go testing practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Table-driven tests looped with t.Run subtests
Running concurrent code tests with -race
Using t.Helper() in assertion helpers
Relying on a built-in assert() function

questions.explanation: Table-driven tests, -race for concurrency, and t.Helper for helpers are idiomatic. Go has no built-in assert; you compare and call t.Error/t.Fatal.

questions.prompt: Why might a benchmark report an unrealistically fast time?

options.text: If the result is never used, the compiler can optimize the work away
Because b.N is always 1
Because benchmarks skip the function body
Because -bench disables timing

questions.explanation: Dead-code elimination can remove work whose result is unused; consume the result (e.g. assign to a package-level sink) to prevent that.
